principles: Assurance equivalence is a hard constraint, not a performance trade.
Concurrency is granted by explicit resource isolation and denied by default.
Process-boundary coverage needs representative sentinels, while behavioral matrices should reuse initialized state.
The canonical suite preserves the first observed failure and emits auditable timing and membership data.
drivers: The measured 1688.9-second feedback loop blocks normal development.
Three long-tail integration suites dominate runtime, so top-level parallelism alone bottoms out at 798.8 seconds.
Existing standalone smoke architecture must remain compatible with black-box validation and DONE-required receipts.
Shared Git and runtime artifacts make unclassified parallelism unsafe.

options.name: A: Top-level worker pool only
cons: Existing retry behavior masks first failures

options.name: B: Resource-aware runner plus internal long-tail optimization
pros: Retains focused standalone smokes and bounded black-box sentinels
cons: Requires manifest migration and equivalence tests

options.name: C: Move long tests out of canonical npm test
cons: Violates the user-confirmed scope and hides rather than removes cost

chosen: B: Resource-aware runner plus internal long-tail optimization
rationale: Only B addresses both measured critical-path cost and safety. It retains published CLI behavior checks while removing repeated initialization that does not add independent assurance.

preMortem.scenario: Parallel tests corrupt or race on a shared Git common directory or fixed path.
preMortem.trigger: Two workers receive entries with an absent or incorrect resource declaration.
preMortem.consequence: Flaky false failures, overwritten evidence, or false PASS results.
preMortem.mitigation: Default unknown entries to serial, validate manifest resource declarations, allocate unique temp roots, and add conflict mutations that must serialize.

preMortem.scenario: The suite meets the budget by silently losing members or mutations.
preMortem.trigger: The new manifest diverges from the frozen canonical inventory or an optimized matrix omits a diagnostic branch.
preMortem.mitigation: Add bidirectional inventory and assertion or mutation failure-matrix equivalence checks; omissions, duplicates, and skips fail closed.

preMortem.scenario: A flaky test fails in parallel then passes under an automatic serial retry.
preMortem.trigger: Legacy two-pass retry semantics remain enabled in the canonical path.
preMortem.consequence: The full-suite receipt records PASS despite an observed failure.
preMortem.mitigation: Canonical mode disables retries and tests assert the first FAIL or TIMEOUT remains terminal with preserved diagnostics.

preMortem.scenario: The benchmark passes only on a warm checkout or leaves child processes behind.
preMortem.trigger: Caching, inherited artifacts, or incomplete timeout cleanup reduce measured time.
preMortem.consequence: The five-minute claim is not reproducible and later runs interfere with each other.
preMortem.mitigation: Run three clean temporary clones after same-material builds, record process and lock telemetry, and mutation-test timeout and process-tree cleanup.
